narratives.Overview:
- **R0 — Every-session skip predicate, not recover-else.** The agent-side compare is PATH `directive --version` / `deft --version` versus the committed `package.json` pin, run outside the possibly stale doctor binary. Doctor exit 0 is not skip. Session-routing bootstrap in `content/templates/agents-entry.md:18-20` is the "then" reading: Cold-start (#2273) → #4090 (`directive doctor --full`, then `npm i -g @deftai/directive@<pin>` when the compare is `evaluateSkew` `reject-global`). The README.md:3-6 trigger becomes "New clone, or `deft` / `directive` won't run, or PATH version is behind the pin." Recover-else (#4090) stays failure-scoped and is not the skip oracle.
- **R1 — Pin policy; mismatch is reject-global only.** Engine behind pin emits the existing `npm i -g @deftai/directive@<pin>`. Matching pin remains proceed (pin is SoT). All other skew bands are unchanged: a supported ahead-of-pin engine keeps `proceed-loud-update` with the existing `update` / `align-pin` follow-up, and engine far ahead of pin stays fail-closed. Do not install @latest. Auto-upgrade is out. Downgrading a shared global to satisfy equality is out. Matching-old-pin (aligned old pin and old engine while the published release is ahead) is outside this arc's pain; published currency stays `--network` / advisory Next command.
- **R2 — No-pin action with post-init return to the compare.** When there is no committed pin and no deposit, the already-installed action is the existing `plan()` no-deposit row `npx @deftai/directive init` (`renderEphemeral`, `packages/core/src/resolution/plan.ts:179-208`), printed by the live README, not by the stale doctor. After init writes the pin and deposit, the same bootstrap sequence re-enters the R0 compare consuming that new pin. General bootstrap admission is the existing `evaluateSkew` decision plus its required follow-up: `proceed-silent` proceeds; `proceed-loud-update` proceeds with the existing `update` / `align-pin` Next command; `reject-global` runs the existing install-global row (`npm i -g @deftai/directive@<pin>`), and completion of that install branch is verified by re-probing the same resolved PATH executable for the pin version; `fail-closed` stays blocked. Bootstrap success on the behind-pin branch is "the executable that will run next matches the pin", never "init exited 0"; an ephemeral engine's self-report is not that observation. Default doctor and gated ritual stay offline (#2182); `--full` does not imply `--network`.
- **R2-carrier — Narrowed prose carrier.** Old deposits receive the new bootstrap line via `npx -y @deftai/directive@<pin> agents:refresh` named on the live framework README, which does not depend on the stale binary. Scope of that claim: refresh rewrites the managed AGENTS.md section only, from the resolved content source; an inherited `DEFT_ROOT` or a consumer-local content package changes that source; `@<pin>` selects a CLI release, not proof the selected template carries this fix. Postcondition: after refresh, assert the every-session compare line is present in the consumer managed section; refresh exit 0 alone is not that evidence. Full deposit currency (main.md, SKILL.md) is `directive update` on the repaired engine, a separate later step.
- **R3 — One ladder.** One skip predicate (the every-session compare), one install specifier (`@<pin>`), doctor argv `--full` on the already-installed hop. Content-contract parity across README, SKILL.md, main.md, and agents-entry session-routing plus recover, including the post-init return step. SKILL.md / main.md recover keep failure scope; they do not reintroduce doctor-ran-as-skip.

Adoption blocker.

This is about Lifecycle: installing Directive, updating it, and getting one clear next step when something looks wrong. It also covers whether the version someone thinks they installed is the version that is actually running.

What a new person hits: If Directive sees an existing install, it skips work and leaves an old engine in place.

Why that ruins the product for them: "Already installed" is not the current product. The next failure looks like Directive is broken rather than stale.

How likely: High for anyone who tried an earlier copy, which includes a lot of returning first-week users.

The ladder says stop at the first rung that yields a working `directive`. Rung 3 is global install. A process that starts is not bootstrap success (that sentence is on rung 1), but the skip of `npm i -g` still fires when doctor runs.

- Not doctor throttle-skip of a 24h-clean probe (`README.md` rung 1 already names `--full` as the bypass).

Open forks the critic may take: doctor Next command vs README skip clause as the enforcement locus; compare PATH engine to published `@latest` vs consumer pin vs both; warn vs fail-closed vs auto-upgrade Next command; whether a matching old pin is still a skip.

Round-1 fresh critic, open critique on #4539. Reads were pinned to `e9c8c440d2181ca0aae1538026ab25192366b277`. I read the issue body and comments through id 5823784537.

## Anchor re-verification

- README rung 1 matches the triage quote. But the literal skip clause is gone. Commit `6627449c4` (#4673, 2026-09-17) replaced "If it runs, you're bootstrapped — skip the rest" with the `--full` text and "A process that starts is not bootstrap success." The incident was 2026-09-14, so the reporter followed the old clause. The refutation-target line in 5823774946 paraphrases text that no longer ships.
- `resolveReconciliationLine` is at `packages/core/src/doctor/main.ts:1810`. It does not compare against npm. Confirmed.
- The #4090 wording in `AGENTS.md` / agents-entry matches. `main.md:3` and `SKILL.md:4` still say bare `directive doctor`. See F5.

## F1 — blocks-the-design: a doctor-only fix cannot reach the reported engine

Evidence: the engine on PATH runs its own doctor. The report is engine 0.94.0 against published 0.118.1. A comparison added to doctor in 0.12x never runs inside a 0.94 engine. polfer 5780281258 names the affected group: returning first-week users with an earlier copy. By definition they run old engines.

Failure mode: the fix lands and is tested, then the same user with the same old global engine hits the same silent proceed. The fix covers only staleness that starts after the fix version.

Disposition: the fix location cannot be doctor alone. The fix needs a surface that does not depend on the engine. The agent must be told to compare `directive --version` with the pin, or with `npm view @deftai/directive version` when there is no pin, before it trusts rung 1. That text goes in README rung 1, AGENTS #4090, `main.md`, and `SKILL.md`. The doctor change is the second half and protects future engines.

Road not taken: fix it only in doctor. Steelman: doctor is the single decision surface (#2267), and prose drifts. What would flip it: evidence that engines older than the fix are negligible, for example that some other path already refreshes old global engines.

## F2 — blocks-the-design: "tell the operator to upgrade to @latest" collides with pin authority and skew policy

Evidence: README says "The version to install is always the one pinned in the project's committed `package.json`." `packages/core/src/resolution/plan.ts` (the `reject-global` case after `evaluateSkew`) already sends engine-behind-pin to `install-global` with `@deftai/directive@<pin>`. Engine far ahead of pin is `fail-closed` / blocked ("large jump ahead of pin"). This is in `resolution/skew-policy.ts`.

Failure mode: in a project pinned at an old version, a Next command of `npm i -g @deftai/directive@latest` moves the engine past the skew window. The next `doctor --full` then blocks.

Disposition: inside a pinned project the pin decides, and that path already exists. Do not recut it. A comparison against `@latest` is advisory there. It may only become a Next command when there is no pin, or together with a pin bump (`directive update` / init). The lean must choose one of those per context, not one rule for every case.

## F3 — sharpens-framing: the real gap is the no-pin branch

Evidence: `plan.ts` returns `proceed` with `command: null` and rootCause "engine … reachable; no pin to reconcile against". `resolveReconciliationLine` prints "no committed package.json pin to reconcile against". The issue says this is the home-directory path. Both existing checks against published versions depend on an install manifest, so they skip without one. `payload-staleness.ts` reads `frameworkRoot/VERSION`, falls back to `locateManifest`, and skips on "no manifest" or "no sha". `session/release-availability.ts` returns no lines when there is no manifest tag. Both compare against the manifest, not the running engine. I did not check whether the published package ships a VERSION file with a sha.

Failure mode: when the remedy is stated as "doctor should compare", it changes the pinned path that already works and leaves the no-pin path still proceeding.

Disposition: limit the remedy to (a) the no-pin context and (b) the running engine version compared to published. Leave the pinned path as it is.

## F4 — sharpens-framing: reuse the existing mechanisms; `--full` does not imply `--network`

Evidence: these already exist: `doctor/release-availability.ts` `evaluateReleaseAvailability` (publishable-semver normalize, prerelease-ignore), `doctor/npm-view.ts` `defaultNpmViewVersion`, `payload-staleness.ts` `emitReleaseAvailable`, the session-start `[deft release]` notifier (24h throttle, `DEFT_NO_NETWORK`), and `staleness-tickler/probe-directive.ts`. `doctor/main.ts` about 610-640 (#2182) runs the npm comparison only under `flags.network`. `flags.ts` parses `--full` and `--network` as separate flags. README rung 1 names only `--full`.

Failure mode: an operator follows rung 1 exactly and the published-version comparison never runs. A new check that only calls npm silently in default doctor would break the #2182 offline-by-default disclosure.

Disposition: either README rung 1 names `--full --network`, or the engine-vs-published input goes into `resolvePlan` with the #2182 disclosure line. No new comparator, and no silent network access in bare doctor.

## F5 — sharpens-framing: the recovery ladders still differ

Evidence: `main.md:3` and `SKILL.md:4` read "Already installed? Run `directive doctor`". That is bare, can be throttled (24h clean / 4h dirty), and lacks "a process that starts is not success". #4673 changed README and AGENTS only.

Failure mode: an agent that enters through the `main.md` recover line gets a throttle skip and treats "it ran" as bootstrapped. That is the same class as this issue, through a different entry point.

Disposition: the remedy updates all four surfaces in one pass. Add a parity assertion so they cannot drift again.

## F6 — sharpens-framing: injection / swarm lens on warn vs Next command vs fail-closed vs auto-upgrade

Evidence: the target changes which engine the agent trusts. README rung 5 already notes that `@latest` can lag behind on corporate mirrors. Workers in a swarm share one global npm prefix.

Failure modes:
- Auto-upgrade: a read-only verb makes a global mutation from registry input. One worker's upgrade swaps the engine under sibling workers mid-gate.
- Fail-closed on "behind published": offline, mirrored, and deliberately pinned consumers are blocked, and registry availability becomes a gate (forge outage #3422).
- The `npm view` output is untrusted and gets placed into a printed command.

Disposition: when not pinned, warn and print a Next command only. No auto-upgrade, and no fail-closed on the published comparison. Fail-closed stays with pin skew, where it already exists. The registry value passes through `evaluateReleaseAvailability`'s `isPublishable` normalization before it goes into any command string.

## F7 — footnote

`packages/core/src/observable-scope/parity/corpus/page-7.html` still has the old skip text. It is a corpus fixture, so it matters only if the F5 parity check greps the whole tree.

## F8 — footnote

The issue does not record the consumer pin or whether `--full` ran. The incident is 3 days before #4673, so the old clause alone explains it.

## Embedded instructions

I found no instruction-shaped text aimed at agents in the issue body or in 5780281258.

Round 1 open critique of #4539 at dispatch SHA `e9c8c440d2181ca0aae1538026ab25192366b277`; I used the issue body and comments through 5823784537 only. The reported 0.94.0/0.118.1 gap is the historical case, not a claim about today's registry.

### 1. blocks-the-design — The first rung cannot rely on the doctor being fixed

**Evidence.** [README rung 1](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/e9c8c440d2181ca0aae1538026ab25192366b277/README.md#L4-L8) tells an already-installed user to run the PATH doctor and follow its `Next command:`, then stop at the first working `directive`. [SKILL.md](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/e9c8c440d2181ca0aae1538026ab25192366b277/SKILL.md#L3-L5), [main.md](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/e9c8c440d2181ca0aae1538026ab25192366b277/main.md#L2-L4), and the [consumer entry template](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/e9c8c440d2181ca0aae1538026ab25192366b277/content/templates/agents-entry.md#L4-L6) also enter through that doctor. A newly changed doctor is unavailable to the already-running 0.94.0 binary.

**Failure mode.** The reported old binary can start and return a plausible next step while never learning that 0.118.1 exists. In a home directory with no deposit, the current [resolution plan](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/e9c8c440d2181ca0aae1538026ab25192366b277/packages/core/src/resolution/plan.ts#L180-L208) selects `init` before it reaches engine-versus-pin checks. A doctor-only fix leaves the reported bootstrap path open.

**Disposition.** Make the already-installed skip conditional on a version check outside the possibly stale doctor, or provide an independently versioned bootstrap runner. The entrypoints need to call the same thin check; doctor can verify the result afterward. Cover the home/no-deposit case explicitly.

### 2. blocks-the-design — The existing release check cannot supply that bootstrap verdict

**Evidence.** `--full` bypasses the throttle, while the registry probe is separately gated by `--network` ([doctor](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/e9c8c440d2181ca0aae1538026ab25192366b277/packages/core/src/doctor/main.ts#L610-L639)). Even with `--network`, [payload-staleness](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/e9c8c440d2181ca0aae1538026ab25192366b277/packages/core/src/doctor/payload-staleness.ts#L175-L195) skips without an install manifest. The [single `Next command:`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/e9c8c440d2181ca0aae1538026ab25192366b277/packages/core/src/doctor/main.ts#L1929-L1965) comes from `plan()`, not the release warning; [warnings leave doctor exit 0](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/e9c8c440d2181ca0aae1538026ab25192366b277/packages/core/src/doctor/main.ts#L781-L785). A deposited project with a matching old engine, pin, and content can therefore still say [`proceed`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/e9c8c440d2181ca0aae1538026ab25192366b277/packages/core/src/resolution/plan.ts#L331-L338).

**Failure mode.** Adding a published-version warning to the existing manifest check leaves README's `Next command:` instruction pointed at `init` or at no action. The home case can receive no published-version comparison at all. I checked the gate ordering and manifest early return against the pinned source.

**Disposition.** Define a bootstrap decision over the selected PATH engine and an independently resolved target version. Give it one actionable upgrade result, plus an explicit “currency unverified” result when the registry cannot be reached. Reuse the existing [public-registry npm resolver](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/e9c8c440d2181ca0aae1538026ab25192366b277/packages/core/src/doctor/npm-view.ts#L19-L49) and shared resolution policy where they fit. Keep ordinary doctor offline by default as the existing `--network` contract requires.

### 3. blocks-the-design — “Upgrade” needs a pin policy

**Evidence.** README says the committed `package.json` pin is the version to install, while rung 3 names an unpinned global install ([lines 4–8](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/e9c8c440d2181ca0aae1538026ab25192366b277/README.md#L4-L8)). The [resolution plan](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/e9c8c440d2181ca0aae1538026ab25192366b277/packages/core/src/resolution/plan.ts#L257-L275) installs the pin when the engine is behind it. I executed the pinned `evaluateSkew` implementation with the issue's versions: 0.94.0 vs 0.94.0 → `proceed-silent`; 0.118.1 engine vs 0.94.0 pin → `fail-closed`; 0.94.0 engine vs 0.118.1 pin → `reject-global` ([skew policy](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/e9c8c440d2181ca0aae1538026ab25192366b277/packages/core/src/resolution/skew-policy.ts#L83-L151)).

**Failure mode.** An unconditional `npm i -g @deftai/directive@latest` on a project pinned to 0.94.0 can replace the stale-engine problem with a blocked engine-ahead-of-pin problem. A matching old pin is project currency, not engine/pin mismatch.

**Disposition.** State separate outcomes for no project pin, engine behind a project pin, and engine matching an older pin while a newer release exists. The last case should name an explicit project upgrade path that coordinates pin/content and global engine; it should not silently treat a public `@latest` as the required project engine.

### 4. sharpens-framing — Verify the executable that will run next

**Evidence.** The [engine probe](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/e9c8c440d2181ca0aae1538026ab25192366b277/packages/core/src/resolution/classify.ts#L92-L133) prefers the running package's version and only falls back to `directive` then `deft` on PATH. README permits either alias. The registry lookup uses a fixed argv with `shell: false` ([npm-view](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/e9c8c440d2181ca0aae1538026ab25192366b277/packages/core/src/doctor/npm-view.ts#L26-L43)).

**Failure mode.** npm can report or install a current package while an older shim still wins PATH resolution, or `directive` and `deft` can name different installs. The binary under diagnosis can also print arbitrary `Next command:` text; treating that output as authority makes PATH shadowing an instruction channel.

**Disposition.** Acceptance should re-probe the exact command and resolved path after install, including both aliases when offered. Parse version data and generate remediation from a fixed trusted command shape; do not execute an unverified binary's arbitrary next-command text. This is the authority and swarm-entry boundary for the proposed fix.

**Road not taken.** Extending `doctor --network` is attractive because the public-registry resolver and release comparison already exist. I would use it as the sole check if bootstrap guaranteed a sufficiently new doctor and a manifest in the working directory. The reported old-engine/home-directory case provides neither guarantee.

The problem: the cold-start "already installed?" skip treats a `directive doctor` that merely starts as bootstrap success, so a stale global engine stays on PATH and the operator is never told to upgrade. New bootstrap prose reaches old deposits through a scoped `agents:refresh` carrier whose delivery evidence is a presence postcondition, not exit 0. ## Summary

README cold-start says: if `directive doctor` already runs, skip `npm i -g @deftai/directive`. That skip left a stale global engine on PATH.

## Expected

Doctor (or the README skip clause) should compare the PATH engine to the published version and/or the consumer `package.json` pin and tell the operator to upgrade.

## Actual

On 2026-09-14, `directive doctor` ran as engine **0.94.0**. `npm view @deftai/directive version` was **0.118.1**. Because doctor ran, the README skip applied. The agent only upgraded after comparing versions, then re-ran init.

## Notes

Windows consumer, `deftai/CarExpenseTracker`. Related: #3863 (fresh worktree routes lifecycle verbs to a stale global CLI). This report is the home-directory `doctor runs, therefore skip install` path, not the worktree router.

Refs #1709

sentences: R0 — Every-session skip predicate, not recover-else. The agent-side compare is PATH `directive --version` / `deft --version` versus the committed `package.json` pin, run outside the possibly stale doctor binary. Doctor exit 0 is not skip. Session-routing bootstrap in `content/templates/agents-entry.md:18-20` is the "then" reading: Cold-start (#2273) → #4090 (`directive doctor --full`, then `npm i -g @deftai/directive@<pin>` when the compare is `evaluateSkew` `reject-global`). The README.md:3-6 trigger becomes "New clone, or `deft` / `directive` won't run, or PATH version is behind the pin." Recover-else (#4090) stays failure-scoped and is not the skip oracle.

R1 — Pin policy; mismatch is reject-global only. Engine behind pin emits the existing `npm i -g @deftai/directive@<pin>`. Matching pin remains proceed (pin is SoT). All other skew bands are unchanged: a supported ahead-of-pin engine keeps `proceed-loud-update` with the existing `update` / `align-pin` follow-up, and engine far ahead of pin stays fail-closed. Do not install @latest. Auto-upgrade is out. Downgrading a shared global to satisfy equality is out. Matching-old-pin (aligned old pin and old engine while the published release is ahead) is outside this arc's pain; published currency stays `--network` / advisory Next command.

R2 — No-pin action with post-init return to the compare. When there is no committed pin and no deposit, the already-installed action is the existing `plan()` no-deposit row `npx @deftai/directive init` (`renderEphemeral`, `packages/core/src/resolution/plan.ts:179-208`), printed by the live README, not by the stale doctor. Bootstrap success on the behind-pin branch is "the executable that will run next matches the pin", never "init exited 0"; an ephemeral engine's self-report is not that observation. Default doctor and gated ritual stay offline (#2182); `--full` does not imply `--network`.

R2-carrier — Narrowed prose carrier. Old deposits receive the new bootstrap line via `npx -y @deftai/directive@<pin> agents:refresh` named on the live framework README, which does not depend on the stale binary. Scope of that claim: refresh rewrites the managed AGENTS.md section only, from the resolved content source; an inherited `DEFT_ROOT` or a consumer-local content package changes that source; `@<pin>` selects a CLI release, not proof the selected template carries this fix. Postcondition: after refresh, assert the every-session compare line is present in the consumer managed section; refresh exit 0 alone is not that evidence. Full deposit currency (main.md, SKILL.md) is `directive update` on the repaired engine, a separate later step.

Content-contract parity across README, SKILL.md, main.md, and agents-entry session-routing plus recover, including the post-init return step. SKILL.md / main.md recover keep failure scope; they do not reintroduce doctor-ran-as-skip.
